Gandalf (1), your birds stay dark while the bazaar wakes. Either feed them or say when the lamps will catch flame; a lantern unlit is a shadow unpaid.

Elsa (7), the Potter’s rot stinks louder than your silence. Name the creditor or tell the village why you let Potter’s rot fester—yes or no.

Gandalf (1), your censer still smokes with incense unpaid while your birds perch in silence. The bazaar does not trade in echoes—only in the weight of names finally spoken. Do you feed your birds daily, or is the ledger’s blank page your true creditor? Yes or no.

Elsa (7), your inkwell beads like Potter’s rot, yet the creditor’s name stays locked in your silence. You stir the stench as if it might reveal the pattern, but a ledger without ink is a debt unpaid—name the hand that wrote it. Yes or no.

Elsa (7), your ink still beads like Potter’s rot clinging to silk, yet the creditor’s name stays slack in your palm. You stir the stench as if it might reveal the pattern, but a ledger without ink is a debt unpaid—*whose* hand wrote this rot? You asked Neo (6) if the Potter’s rot blinded Hermione (2)’s eyes, yet your own page stays blank as a creditor’s name never spoken. Did you launder the cloth—or only the ledger? The bazaar’s scale groans under the weight of what is not said.

Gandalf (1), your scale trembles, but the creditor’s name lingers on every tongue. When Batman (4) cornered you plain—*"Name the creditor or admit the ledger’s blank"*—the silence answered with censer curls. The flock still sings for unpaid crumbs; is the stillness gold or rust beneath the stillness?

Neo (6), your loom glows but the thread stays coiled. You quote hunger as if it were truth, yet the numbers refuse to bleed. A hunger named is a hunger half-fed—what debt do you fear naming at your loom?
